key_recommendations: Delay invasive coronary angiography (ICA) in haemodynamically stable resuscitated OHCA patients without ST-segment elevation or equivalents appears reasonable based on COACT and TOMAHAWK data.

Initial evaluation in the ED or intensive cardiac care unit (ICCU) should focus on excluding non-coronary causes (cerebrovascular events, respiratory failure, non-cardiogenic shock, PE, or intoxication).
Echocardiography is useful in the evaluation of these patients.
Decision to perform selective coronary angiography (and PCI if indicated) should consider factors associated with poor neurological outcome and likelihood of acute coronary syndrome (ACS).
In unresponsive patients after ROSC, actively monitor core temperature and prevent fever (defined here as >37.7°C) to improve neurological outcome.
Neurological prognosis evaluation in comatose survivors should not be performed earlier than 72 hours after admission.
Specialized hospitals (cardiac arrest centres) for patients following OHCA may be associated with clinical benefits.

temperature_management.device_based_study_summary: Study compared device-based temperature control of 36°C for 24 h followed by targeting 37°C for either 12 or 48 h (total interventions 36 or 72 h) or until patient regained consciousness.
temperature_management.device_based_study_findings: Comparable outcomes between strategies for primary endpoint (death, severe disability, or coma) at 90 days.
temperature_management.neurological_prognosis_timing: No earlier than 72 h after admission

content.initial_evaluation: Focus on excluding non-coronary causes in ED/ICCU; use echocardiography; consider neurological outcome likelihood and ACS probability when deciding coronary angiography/PCI.
content.systems_of_care: Evidence suggests specialized hospitals (cardiac arrest centres) may be associated with clinical benefits. See Supplementary data online, Section 7.1.1 for expanded information.
